title: Local observability bootstrap patterns and TF guardrails
content:
Purpose and audience:
This doc is a pragmatic bootstrap + guardrails playbook for getting a minimal, safe observability stack into a customer VPC or on-prem cluster. Target readers: platform engineers, SREs, and infra-focused solutions engineers delivering Private deployments.

Goals (minimal viable observability):
- Collect host and application metrics (Prometheus-compatible)
- Collect traces and logs via OTEL Collector
- Provide dashboards (Grafana provisioning) and alerting with safe defaults
- Ensure predictable storage and backpressure behavior under load
- Terraform-first delivery with small, auditable modules and safety checks

High-level pattern overview:
1) Control plane provisioning (customer-managed): network, KMS secrets store, s3-compatible long-term storage (object store), and a minimal operator namespace.
2) Core telemetry plane: managed Prometheus (or Thanos sidecar for long-term retention), Grafana with provisioning via config files, and one or more OTEL Collector deployments split by ingestion role (ingest, transform, egress).
3) Safety and guardrails enforced by Terraform modules and admission policies (resource quotas, mutating webhook to inject scrape configs).

Terraform module boundaries (recommended):
- network-bootstrap: VPC subnets, routing, nat gateways, security groups scoped to telemetry endpoints
- secrets-store-integration: KMS key alias + IAM role bindings for collectors and Prometheus to fetch credentials
- prometheus-core: StatefulSet or operator install, serviceMonitor CRDs enabled, retention/storage config, scrape-relay sidecar options
- grafana-provision: provisioning configmap, datasources, initial dashboards, admin user integration with SSO
- otel-collector: deployment templates for ingest/transform/egress pipelines, processors and exporters wired to secrets-store
- log-shipping: log-forwarder (fluent/fluent-bit) helm values and sink configs (local disk buffer + object store archive)

Terraform guardrails (must-haves):
- enforce immutable tags and owner metadata for every resource
- default resource requests/limits and QoS classes for collector pods
- prevent creation of public-facing endpoints (explicit boolean to opt-in for public access)
- enforce encrypted remote state and automatic state locking (DynamoDB/GCS lock)
- require a canary boolean to enable rolling upgrades of telemetry components

OTEL Collector pipeline sketches (ingest/transform/egress):
- Ingest: receivers: prometheus, otlp/grpc, fluentforward; processors: batch, memory_limiter; exporters: kafka or local_file (for debug)
- Transform (optional): resource and attribute processors to strip PII, normalize service.name, add tenant labels
- Egress: exporters: prometheusremotewrite (to downstream prometheus or remote_write gateway), otlp/otlphttp to tracing backend, s3file for log archive
Notes: configure memory_limiter and retry_on_failure carefully; enable backpressure to avoid OOM.

Prometheus specifics:
- Use serviceMonitors rather than raw scrape_configs when possible (k8s-friendly)
- Retention: short-term local retention (7-14d) + remote_write to object store/Thanos for long-term
- Recording rules: ship a small, agreed set (latency_p50/p95, error_rate, qps) rather than heavy cardinality rules
- Scrape intervals: default 30s for infra, 15s for high-card apps, but enforce upper bound to prevent overload

Grafana provisioning and dashboards:
- Provision via configmaps in TF module (datasource to local Prometheus/remote_write reader)
- Provide tenant-aware dashboard templates and one evaluation dashboard for rollout verification (ingest rate, queue depth, processing latency)
- Lock provisioning to read-only for non-admins; include a managed dashboard refresh job to reconcile drift

Log shipping and archival patterns:
- Fluent-bit on nodes with local disk buffer (spill to filesystem), forward to OTEL collector or directly to object store via multipart uploads
- Control retention via lifecycle policies in object store (30/90/365d depending on compliance)
- Support on-prem customers that cannot use external object stores by enabling NFS/baremetal SMB gateway options

Upgrade and rollback strategy (Prometheus/Grafana/OTEL):
- Canary path: deploy new version to 10% of replicas or a dedicated canary namespace; run synthetic scrapes and evals for 24–48h
- Metric-level gating: compare recording rule outputs and alert rates vs baseline. If regression > 5% for key metrics, autorollback
- Config rollout: use ConfigMap hash annotation on pods to force rolling restarts; prefer operator-driven upgrades where available
- Database migration caution: do not change TSDB retention or block format without explicit migration step and snapshot

Operational playbook: quick checks after bootstrap
- kubectl get pods -n telemetry -o wide
- curl -fsS http://prometheus.internal.svc:9090/-/ready || echo PROM READY FAIL
- grafana-cli --version (or curl grafana health endpoint)
- otel-collector logs: kubectl logs -n telemetry deploy/otel-collector-ingest | grep -i "backpressure\|OOM\|retry"
- check object store uploads: aws s3 ls s3://telemetry-archive/ --human-readable --summarize (or s3-compatible cli)

Validation tests (automated):
- synthetic load: fire 10k scrape targets at 20s intervals for 30m and measure ingestion success
- end-to-end trace test: generate traces from a demo app and assert they arrive in tracing backend within 10s
- log fidelity check: tail N logs from source and ensure 99.9% presence in archive index

Danger signs and mitigations:
- sudden scrape latency spike -> reduce scrape cadence, enable extra scrape relays
- OTEL collector OOM bursts -> increase memory_limiter thresholds, add a throttling processor, scale out collectors
- Disk pressure on nodes -> enable throttled log buffer to object store and set retention TTLs

Delivery checklist for solution engineers (turnkey):
- [ ] Confirm network egress requirements and KMS access
- [ ] Provision TF workspace with encrypted remote state and locking
- [ ] Apply network-bootstrap and secrets-store-integration modules
- [ ] Deploy prometheus-core with a single canonical serviceMonitor per app
- [ ] Deploy otel-collector ingest pipeline and validate trace/metric flow
- [ ] Provision grafana and import evaluation dashboard
- [ ] Run validation tests and capture baseline metrics

Open questions / future work:
- Explore lightweight remote_write gateway to reduce cross-VPC egress charges
- Standardize on a single log archival schema for better search compatibility across on-prem customers
- Investigate sidecarless scrape relays for very high-density hosts

Appendix: example minimal TF variable shape (informal)
- prometheus_core: { replicas = 3, retention = "14d", remote_write_endpoint = "https://rw.example/", tls_mode = "mtls" }
- grafana: { admin_email = "ops@example.com", provision_dashboards = true }
- otel_collector: { pipeline_count = 2, memory_limit_mb = 1024 }

Notes: This is a working draft intended to be used as the starting point for customer engagements. Many recommendations assume the operator can modify cluster-level policies; where that is not possible we recommend swapping to sidecar-forwarding and smaller collection footprints. Feedback welcome — add comments or ping @Aisha on Slack.
